h1: The 6 Best Printers with Cheap Ink of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers with Cheap Ink: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six refillable tank printers that keep ink costs low, compared on ink supply, features and fit for home or office use.
summary: The HP Smart Tank 5101 is the best pick for low ink cost, with two years of ink included. The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the best cheap-to-run entry printer, and the ET-4800 and ET-4950 suit offices that print daily.
intro: A cheap printer with expensive cartridges is a trap, because the ink often costs more than the machine within a year. The buyers who save money pick a refillable tank printer and pay a bit more up front.

We reviewed eight tank printers and ranked six on the spec sheet, looking at how much ink ships in the box, how large the refill system is, and what features justify the price tier. Duplicate colour variants were folded together.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: Two years of ink included in the box keeps early costs close to zero.
products.description:
The HP Smart Tank 5101 is a refillable tank machine whose listing bundles two years of ink, with scan and copy built in. It has a compact footprint compared with larger tank models and wireless printing on 2.4GHz only.

It ranks first because the bundled ink is the clearest cost saving here. The Epson models below match its tank design but the listing highlights bottles for setup rather than a long supply.

Buy it for a home that prints steadily. The caveat is that it has no automatic document feeder and Wi-Fi is 2.4GHz only.
products.idealFor: Households that print every week and hate buying ink.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer (Black)
products.verdict: A compact EcoTank with setup bottles in the box and a low entry price.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 prints, scans and copies wirelessly in a compact body, with ink bottles included for setup. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks second because the HP 5101 lists a longer included supply, but the ET-2800 is a proven simple choice. You give up a feeder.

Pick it for a student or light home printing. The caveat is that scanning a stack of pages is manual.
products.skipIf: You need Ethernet or a feeder.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A feeder, fax and Ethernet in the same $100 to $200 tier.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 has an automatic document feeder, fax, Ethernet, scanner and copier, with wireless and wired connectivity, all in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks third because it needs more space and more bottles than the entry models, but it packs the most office tools for the money.

Pick it for a small office. The caveat is that fax is a feature many homes never use.
products.idealFor: Home offices that scan and copy a lot.
products.skipIf: You only print a few pages.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Refills rated up to three years, with a touchscreen and feeder.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-4950 lists ink refills rated for up to three years, an automatic document feeder, a 2.4-inch touchscreen and 18 ppm print speed.

It ranks fourth because the upfront cost is higher than the ET-4800 for similar office features. The long ink rating is what justifies it.

Pick it for daily printing. The caveat is the $200 to $500 price tier.

products.name: Canon PIXMA G620 Wireless MegaTank Photo All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: A Canon MegaTank that keeps photo printing cheap.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA G620 is a MegaTank photo model with refillable reservoirs, covering copy and scan duties plus Wi-Fi and Alexa voice support.

It ranks fifth because it costs more than the Epson entry models and has no feeder in the listing. Photo-focused output is the draw.

Choose it if you print photos regularly. The caveat is the $200 to $500 price tier.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A plain compact EcoTank for everyday pages.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is a small tank printer for everyday pages at home, with Wi-Fi and basic scan and copy.

It ranks last because the ET-2800 lists included setup bottles and the listing here is thin. The two are close.

Pick it for simple needs. The caveat is that it has no feeder in the listing.

whatMatters.detail: A tank printer fills from bottles instead of using small cartridges, and bottles hold far more ink per dollar. The machine costs more upfront, so it pays off for regular printers. Check the title for EcoTank, MegaTank or Smart Tank.
Some listings include a long supply of ink, like the HP Smart Tank 5101's two years. That saves money early on. Look for wording about included ink in the title or bullets.
Savings grow with volume. A printer used a few times a year may never repay a higher price. Estimate your monthly pages before choosing a tier.
A feeder helps scanning and copying, and the ET-4800 and ET-4950 list one. Without it you scan page by page. Check the bullets.
Some printers connect only on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, which matters on modern routers. The HP 5101 lists this limit. Check the connectivity line before buying.

faq.q: Are tank printers really cheaper to run?
faq.a: Usually, for regular printers. Bottles hold more ink per dollar than cartridges, though the printer costs more upfront.
Buying the cheapest printer and ignoring ink cost. Pick a tank model instead.

faq.q: Is the ET-4950 worth it over the ET-4800?
faq.a: For daily printing, yes, thanks to the touchscreen and long ink rating. Otherwise the ET-4800 saves money.

faq.q: How do I set up a tank printer?
faq.a: Fill each tank with the matching bottle and follow the on-screen alignment steps.
Print something regularly. Long idle periods can dry ink, so run a test page now and then.

faq.q: Does the HP work on 5GHz Wi-Fi?
faq.a: The listing says 2.4GHz only, so use that band or a dual-band router.

finalTake: The HP Smart Tank 5101 is the smartest pick for cheap ink thanks to two years included in the box. The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 suits light users, the ET-4800 suits offices, and the ET-4950 suits heavy use. Choose a tank model and ink stops being the expensive part.
